gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: It is one of the most impressive buildings ___ I have ever seen.
gaps.explanation: After superlative expressions, 'that' is the standard relative pronoun in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: The hotel, ___ rates include breakfast, is fully booked for the conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' marks possession even for things: the hotel whose rates…

gaps.sentence: The theatre ___ we saw the premiere has been restored beautifully.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' relates to a place: the theatre where we saw…
'Who's' is the contraction of 'who is'; 'whose' shows possession and cannot stand before an adjective alone.

gaps.sentence: The house ___ windows were broken has now been sold.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose windows' — the windows belong to the house.

gaps.sentence: The stadium ___ the final will be held holds ninety thousand people.
gaps.hint: place adverb inside the relative clause
gaps.explanation: 'Where' stands for 'in which place'; 'which' would leave the clause without a subject or object.

gaps.sentence: The candidate ___ speech impressed us most got the job.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose speech' — the speech belonged to the candidate.
